judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional preamble identifying the Indian company, the employee and an Effective Date; nothing in it carries two reasonable meanings beyond OCR noise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names only Ajuba Solutions (India) Pvt Ltd as 'the Company', yet Section 2.4 makes 'the Company' liable for payouts triggered by MiraMed's transactions and Section 7.5 directs notices to a Michigan entity, so the identity of the obligor is not perfectly coherent across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Business' is defined by an open 'including but not limited to' list and by the wholly elastic phrase 'such other entities serviced by the Company at any time during the Employment Term', a classic general-vs-specific scope problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term feeds the 'Company Technology' definition (1.2) and Article 4's assignment obligation, so its reach matters elsewhere, but I found no provision it directly contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition turns on what is 'known to the Employee' as a result of employment and 'relates to the Business', both undelimited, and the surviving text is grammatically incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1 requires assignment of Company Technology 'conceived, developed or acquired during the Employment Term', a narrower trigger than 'known to the Employee', leaving a gap between the definition and the operative assignment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All information, in whatever form, regarding the Company and the Business, and their clients, including without limitation' followed by nine enumerated categories is exactly the general catch-all against specifics that invites an ejusdem generis fight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1's carve-outs for public-domain and third-party-sourced information cabin the definition rather than contradict it, and I found no other conflicting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A client of the Company' defines one undefined word by another, but the term is so short and conventional that little turns on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: I could not find 'Customer' used anywhere in the operative text — there is no non-solicitation covenant — so the definition is orphaned, an oddity but not an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed commencement and a fixed 31 December 2013 end date with an express cross-reference to Article 6; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Term ends early only 'pursuant to Article 6', yet Section 6.1 adds termination 'upon the consummation of a Liquidity Event', a Section 2.4 concept, and 2.4(b) contemplates the relationship continuing past termination, so the fit is imperfect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard calendar-year definition with a change-of-fiscal-year escape; the OCR is damaged but the drafting is ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Fiscal Year' does not appear to be used in any operative provision — Sections 6.3 and 6.4 speak of a 'calendar year' instead — which is a loose end rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition breaks off mid-sentence ('any corporation, company, partnership, other entity or'), so as it stands it is literally incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Person' appears nowhere else in the surviving operative text, so the incompleteness has no downstream consequence I could identify.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Duties are fixed only by reference to what a President 'customarily' performs and to an unattached 'Schedule 2.1', and the exclusivity covenant ('will not, whether or not during business hours, be engaged in any other business or professional activity') is broad and undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.2(b) makes failure to perform 'consistent with the provisions of Schedule 2.1' a Cause ground and Section 6.4(a) measures Good Reason by duties 'as outlined in Section 2.1', so a missing or vague Schedule destabilises two other operative provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Base Salary and the US$18,800 Allowance are stated numerically, but the benefits sentence lets the Company modify or discontinue benefits 'at the sole discretion of the Company', and the salary figure itself is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 6.2, 6.3, 6.4 and 6.5 all measure payments by 'the Base Salary and Bonus', yet this compensation section as it survives defines no Bonus, leaving a defined-benefit term hanging across Article 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses' with a records requirement is boilerplate reimbursement language; nothing here has a genuine second meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is subordinated to 'Company policies' and does not touch the termination or bonus machinery; I found no provision it conflicts with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three-tier formula produces awkward boundaries and the payout is conditioned on delivering a 'Separation Agreement and Release of Liability ... in the form attached hereto' that does not appear to be attached, plus the 'in lieu of any amounts otherwise payable ... on account of any prior agreements' carve-out is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 says employment terminates 'upon the consummation of a Liquidity Event', which sits directly against 2.4(a)'s requirement that the Employee be 'employed by the Company at the time of consummation', and Section 7.8's supersession of prior agreements pulls against the 'prior agreements' sentence here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 1.75% tail payment is stated definitely, but it is silent on how it interacts with the tiered percentages in (a) and on whether a release is likewise required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a right to payment after employment ends, which conflicts with 2.4(a)'s employment condition and with 2.4(d)'s closing sentence conditioning deferred payment on 'remaining as an employee of the Company at the time that payment is due'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (ii) strings three transactions together before a single qualifier about Tony Mira's family retaining 50% of the surviving entity, so it is genuinely unclear whether that qualifier attaches only to the merger or to the sale limbs too; the express carve-out of MiraMed Revenue Group also invites expressio unius argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition drives Section 6.1's automatic termination and both limbs of Section 2.4, so any ambiguity here propagates, though I found no flat contradiction with another clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The build-up of 'total amount of cash and fair market value of other property paid or payable ... plus, without duplication' indebtedness, repurchases and distributions is fragmentary, and a condition about deferred payments has been dropped into the middle of a valuation definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That condition — payment 'conditioned on you remaining as an employee of the Company at the time that payment is due' — cannot be reconciled with 2.4(b), which promises a payout up to 12 months after employment has ended, nor with 6.1's termination on consummation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics are precise (Wall Street Journal rate, 10-trading-day average), but the clause repeatedly uses a capitalised 'Transaction' that is nowhere defined in the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined trigger elsewhere is 'Liquidity Event' (2.4(c)), so 'the date a Transaction is consummated' has to be read across from a different defined term to work at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation is absolute and perpetual with four exceptions, the last of which breaks off ('to the extent disclosure is ...'), and 'any portion thereof' extends a very broad definition further.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with 1.3 and 3.2, and Section 7.7 keeps it alive after termination, so I found no conflicting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward return-and-delete obligation on termination; the only softness is what counts as 'control' of Confidential Information.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 4.2 for Company Technology and fits 3.1 and 7.7 without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except for legitimate business purposes' is an exception broad enough to swallow the confidentiality promise it qualifies, and 'legitimate' is exactly the kind of undefined evaluative word a court has to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the only obligation running against the Company in Article 3 and I found nothing elsewhere that contradicts it, though it sits oddly beside the Employee's absolute obligation in 3.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Upon the Company's request ... Employee shall assign' is a promise to assign rather than a present assignment, and 'relating in any way to the Business' is a very wide reach qualified only by 'to the extent permitted by law'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The scope here ('conceived, developed or acquired during the Employment Term') does not match the 'Company Technology' definition in 1.2, which turns on what is known to the Employee, so the two do not line up cleanly.
